newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker, sell off on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker, sell off on dollar.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Friday after being dragged down by a tumble in the Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"The bond market has caught the flu, with about 50 percent of the traders," said ABN AMRO Bank Canada analyst Andrew Pyle. Both Pyle and TD Securities Inc fixed-income research director Jim Webber pointed to weakness in the Canadian currency. "The currency has not been doing that well," Webber said. Canada's 30-year bond lost C$1.00 to end at C$107.20 to yield 7.375 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The spread between two bonds widened to 49 basis points from about 45 basis points at Thursday's close.
Canada's dollar weakened to end at C$1.3492 (US$0.7412) on Friday from Thursday's opening mark of C$1.3390 (US$0.7468), hit by profit-taking after a two-week rally, analysts said.

Pyle said North American markets will stay nervous ahead of the fourth quarterly U.S. Employment Cost Index statistics, out on Tuesday. U.S. Federal Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan voiced concerns about rising wages this week, which means market players will be eyeing Tuesday's barometer of labor costs.
A Reuters survey of analysts predicted an average of 0.9 percent, compared to 0.6 percent in the third quarter.
"The bond market is probably on a heightened state of alert," Pyle added.
Statistics out of Canada next week will include November's fixed-weight hourly earnings on Tuesday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.80 to C$101.95 to yield 6.724 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to nine basis points from six basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash t-bill traded with a yield of 2.86 percent against the U.S. bill yielded 5.16 percent.
